hero.title: MirDB

codeExample.description: Connect with any Memcached client. Here are the basics over the text protocol:
codeExample.snippet:
# Start the server
mirdb-server --port 11211

# In another shell, use any memcached client:
set hello 0 0 5
world
# STORED

get hello
# VALUE hello 0 5
# world
# END

add counter 0 0 1
0
# STORED

replace hello 0 0 5
MirDB
# STORED

delete counter
# DELETED

whyMirDB.difference: MirDB writes every value to durable disk storage — your data stays persistent across restarts, where Memcached lives purely in memory and forgets on shutdown.
MirDB chooses simplicity and Memcached protocol compatibility over Redis's much larger command surface — a tiny wire format your existing clients already speak.
MirDB ships with a network protocol out of the box, so any Memcached client can talk to it; RocksDB is an embedded library you have to wrap yourself.
